The longest river in the United States is the Missouri River [d1][d8]. Wikipedia's Missouri River article explicitly calls it "the nation's longest," rising in the eastern Centennial Mountains [d8], and the List of Longest Rivers of the United States ranks it #1 at 2,341 miles (3,768 km), just ahead of the Mississippi River at 2,340 miles [d1]. The USGS, measuring from source to mouth, gives the Missouri River an even longer figure of 2,540 miles (4,088 km), placing it 200 miles ahead of the Mississippi [d5]. The Missouri flows through seven states — Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Iowa, Kansas, and Missouri — before joining the Mississippi River near St. Louis [d2][d5], and together the Missouri-Mississippi system forms the fourth-longest river system in the world [d3][d8].
